title: Psalm 83: When the Nations Conspire
summary: The psalmist begs God not to stay silent while a coalition of surrounding nations plots to wipe Israel off the map. He names ten enemies, recalls God's victories over Midian, Sisera, and Jabin in the days of the judges, and asks God to scatter the enemies like chaff and cover them with shame. The prayer ends with the hope that they will come to know that the LORD alone is Most High over all the earth.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 83

line: The psalmist begs God not to stay silent while the surrounding nations plot against Israel, and ends hoping that they will come to know the LORD alone as Most High.
guide: When you feel surrounded, you may ask God not to be silent. But let the ending shape what you want: not that those against you vanish, but that they come to know the LORD. Can you pray that for the people who stand against you?

stanzas.title: A plea for God to break his silence
The enemies plot to erase Israel
The roll call of the alliance
Do to them as you did in the days of the judges
Scatter them like chaff, pursue them with storm
Let them be ashamed and know the LORD is Most High

verses.t: A song. A Psalm of Asaph. O God, be not silent; be not speechless; be not still, O God.
See how Your enemies rage, how Your foes have reared their heads.
With cunning they scheme against Your people and conspire against those You cherish,
saying, “Come, let us erase them as a nation; may the name of Israel be remembered no more.”
For with one mind they plot together, they form an alliance against You—
the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, of Moab and the Hagrites,
of Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, of Philistia with the people of Tyre.
Even Assyria has joined them, lending strength to the sons of Lot. Selah
Do to them as You did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the River Kishon,
who perished at Endor and became like dung on the ground.
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, “Let us possess for ourselves the pastures of God.”
Make them like tumbleweed, O my God, like chaff before the wind.
As fire consumes a forest, as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,
so pursue them with Your tempest, and terrify them with Your storm.
Cover their faces with shame, that they may seek Your name, O LORD.
May they be ever ashamed and terrified; may they perish in disgrace.
May they know that You alone, whose name is the LORD, are Most High over all the earth.
